summary: CheckYourself audited itself after the v1.7.0 hardening pass. That pass found and fixed real defects in the tool — a score-gaming vector, a secret-scanner miss, out-of-tree symlink reads, an MCP path-confinement gap, silent truncation, and a CI script-injection sink — then re-earned 100/100 under stricter, harder-to-game scoring.

language_mode.reason: The product determines candidate second-language support at run time and asks before using it.

detected_stack: Deterministic detector engine with stable rule IDs

coverage.evidence: README, START_HERE, and bootstrap define audience, outputs, and approval workflow.
CLI describe, manifest, and docs define the file-first architecture.
Dashboard template, smoke check, rendered dashboard, and screenshot exist.
No hosted backend, upload endpoint, or webhook receiver.
No auth, account, role, session, or admin runtime.
No database, migrations, or persisted user records.
No multitenant runtime or user data boundary.
Gitleaks clean; detection and redaction share one token list; scanner never reads through symlinks; one reviewed suppression in .checkyourself.yml.
Symlink and MCP path containment added; composite action hardened against script injection; redaction covered by tests.
Local-first, no telemetry, and docs warn against sharing sensitive data.
60 unit tests, schema validation, py_compile, gitleaks, and MCP smoke pass.
Strict CI on both remotes validates public shape, CLI/diff contracts, MCP wrapper, tests, and gitleaks; Dependabot covers actions and docker.
Public GitHub and Forgejo repos are live; git history is rollback for static repo changes.
No cloud runtime or IaC ships in the public product.
Progressive context loading and dashboard opt-in are documented.
No service workload; context-size control is documented.
SUPPORT.md, SECURITY.md, issue template, and Actions logs define triage surfaces.
Static open-source repo; recovery is git history, cloneability, and future releases.
AGENTS, rules, coverage matrix, scoring method, schemas, and fixture govern behavior.
Learning templates, output, changelog, and dogfood reports tie findings to learning.

findings.title: Thin or omitted coverage could reach a perfect, high-confidence score
findings.plain_risk: The score CheckYourself sells as hard-to-game could be faked with empty evidence.
findings.next_step: Anti-gaming scoring with a regression test guards it.

findings.title: Secret scanner stopped after the first hits, missing later credentials in a file
findings.plain_risk: A committed credential below an earlier hit could go unreported.
findings.next_step: Full-file scan plus a multi-credential regression test.

findings.title: Symlinked files were read out-of-tree
findings.plain_risk: An adversarial project could point a source-looking file at host secrets and have them scanned.
findings.next_step: Symlinks are skipped and disclosed in scan_limits.

findings.title: MCP scan accepted any host path and ignored misspelled arguments
findings.plain_risk: An agent could scan the wrong directory, or anywhere on the host, while reporting success.
findings.next_step: Scan-root confinement and strict argument validation.

findings.title: The 6,000-file scan cap truncated silently
findings.plain_risk: A large project could get a partial scan that looked complete.

findings.title: The composite GitHub Action interpolated inputs into shell
findings.plain_risk: A consumer wiring untrusted inputs could hit a script-injection sink.
findings.next_step: Inputs are passed through environment variables.

remediation_waves.goal: Truncation disclosure and CI input hardening

next_approval: No approval batch remains. The v1.7.0 hardening pass is complete and released on both remotes.

learning_priorities.concept: A score is only as honest as it is hard to game
learning_priorities.plain_english: Absence of evidence is not proof of safety. A maturity score must treat missing or hand-waved coverage as Unknown, never as an automatic pass.
learning_priorities.why: The v1.7.0 audit found that thin or omitted coverage could reach a perfect, high-confidence score.
learning_priorities.do_this_next: When you add a scoring path, ask how someone would fake a perfect result, then close that path.
learning_priorities.success_signal: Thin coverage scores low; only complete, evidenced coverage reaches 100/high.
learning_priorities.why_this_source_is_trusted: This is the repository's canonical scoring contract.
learning_priorities.youtube_title: Evals in Action: From Frontier Research to Production Applications

learning_priorities.concept: Treat the input you scan as hostile
learning_priorities.plain_english: A tool that reads untrusted projects can be turned against its host: a symlinked file or an unconfined path becomes an exfiltration primitive.
learning_priorities.why: The v1.7.0 audit found out-of-tree symlink reads and an unconfined MCP scan path.
learning_priorities.do_this_next: Never follow symlinks, confine every read and write to the target tree, and disclose anything you skip.
learning_priorities.success_signal: An adversarial fixture cannot make the scanner read or report files outside the project.
learning_priorities.why_this_source_is_trusted: OWASP maintains the canonical reference for path-traversal classes.
